definition: VoxForge is a free speech corpus and acoustic model repository for open source speech recognition engines.
details: VoxForge was set up to collect transcribed speech to create a free GPL speech corpus in order to be uses with open source speech recognition engines. The speech audio files will be 'compiled' into acoustic models for use with open source speech recognition engines such as Julius, ISIP, and Sphinx and HTK (note: HTK has distribution restrictions). VoxForge has used LibriVox as a source of audio data since 2007.

explainer.lead: VoxForge is a free speech corpus and acoustic model repository for open-source speech recognition engines. It matters because it collects transcribed speech to create a free GPL speech corpus usable with open-source recognisers.

tiers.eli5: It's a public collection of recorded speech that anyone can use to teach computers to understand words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compile the contributed audio into acoustic models for engines such as Julius, ISIP, Sphinx, and HTK; a pitfall is that HTK carries distribution restrictions, and corpus quality depends on volunteer contributions.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a free speech corpus and acoustic model repository; transcribed speech is compiled into acoustic models for open-source engines, with LibriVox used as an audio source since 2007. HTK has distribution restrictions.

explainer.example: A developer downloads VoxForge audio, compiles an acoustic model, and uses it with the Sphinx recogniser.
